registered_note: Registered before any E3 batch result. Development data: one E2 run (p0_W0g_task9_seed28_d1) used to debug and time the pipeline; its values informed only the pipeline choices listed under conventions_not_derived, and the sensitivity analysis repeats the primary family without it
question: Do the output-layer root corrections that carried a dynamic cost in E1 (W0X) and E2 (W0g) also raise the load on the lumbar spine, the neck and the shoulders, and do they change working posture
interpretation: Registered before the batch. Upper-body loads of output-corrected motions measure how far the correction pushes the motion beyond what a human body can produce, not an ergonomic risk a worker would bear: at the corrected windows the required joint moments exceed the muscles and the reserves carry the excess, so joint reactions there are lower bounds. A supported primary hypothesis therefore means that output-layer correction distorts an ergonomic assessment of the generated motion; absolute load levels are model-dependent and only paired differences within one model are interpreted
data: Every run evaluated by E1 (config/e1_biomech_20261101.json, 1080 M2 runs) and E2 (config/e2_biomech_20261102.json, 576 P0 runs); generated motions read only, no new generation

pipeline.posture: From the generated joint rotations: trunk relative to pelvis and neck relative to chest as Z-X-Y angles, trunk and head inclination from vertical, upper-arm elevation relative to the chest, head angular speed; mean, |.| 95th percentile, RMS and ISO 11226 zone fractions over the trimmed motion
pipeline.lumbar: FBLS full-body lumbar spine model (Raabe & Chaudhari 2016, 324 Thelen muscles) with the E1 pipeline: per-segment scaling to 75 kg, joint-centre IK with axial spine markers (weight 0.3) registered in a lumbar-locked first second, pelvis coordinates unclamped, 6 Hz filter, contact-constrained ground reactions, inverse dynamics, static optimization (activation squared, reserves 1000 pelvis / 1 lumbar and legs / 200 arms as the model release), joint reactions at L5-S1 ... L1-L2 on the caudal-most child vertebra in its own frame; shoulder resultant moment from the FBLS inverse dynamics
pipeline.neck: HYOID head-neck model (Mortensen et al. 2018, 72 Millard muscles, rigid tendon) with the impact actuators removed, head-neck masses scaled by 75/79.54 kg, the 6-DOF base driven by the generated chest; per-frame least-squares fit of the six independent neck coordinates to the generated neck and head rotations relative to the chest (T1 at the generated neck joint); inverse dynamics, static optimization (reserves 1e4 base / 1 N m neck), joint reactions at C7-T1 (on C7) and C0-C1 (on the skull) driven by the static-optimization controls

validity.lumbar: As E1: IK RMS <= 0.03 m, IK max <= 0.10 m, required vertical force within 1 +- 0.02 BW; joint-reaction finite on >= 95% of frames
validity.neck: Chest fit <= 1 deg, T1 fit <= 5 mm, C2 and skull orientation fit RMS <= 2 deg, neck coordinates at a range limit on <= 20% of frames, joint-reaction finite on >= 95% of frames
validity.exclusion: Invalid records excluded pairwise per region; reserves are outcomes, not validity criteria

primary.family: Six hypotheses, Holm-adjusted at 0.05 over the exact sign-flip p values; each also requires the lower 95% interval bound > 0

metrics.shoulder: shoulder resultant moment RMS (N m/kg), mean of both sides

contrasts.e1: W0X - C0, pooled over offsets 0.1/0.5/1.0 m
contrasts.e2: W0g - G4, pooled over offsets 0.5/1.0 m

primary.pooling: One difference per task-seed-offset, equal-weight task means, cluster t interval (G = 24, G - 1 df), exact sign-flip p

secondary: E1: W0 - C0, XFh - C0, XFo - C0, W0X - W0; E2: G4 - G0, G4W - G4, W0g - G0 on every region metric
L4-L5 and L1-L2 compression, L5-S1 shear and peak, fraction of frames above the NIOSH 3400 N limit
lumbar flexion / lateral bending / axial rotation moments; trunk and neck muscle-group activations, muscle effort, reserve RMS
C0-C1 compression, neck shear, neck coordinate moments
posture endpoints and ISO 11226 zone fractions
validity by arm; sensitivity of the primary family without the development run
conventions_not_derived: Static optimization at 10 Hz for FBLS (about 4 s per frame for 324 muscles) and 50 Hz for HYOID
Neck fit, limit and joint-reaction validity thresholds

Joint reactions of FBLS from the static-optimization forces file; of HYOID from the static-optimization controls with rigid-tendon muscles (the forces-file override returned NaN on most HYOID frames; converting FBLS to Millard muscles added passive forces of several hundred N per hip flexor)
Axial spine marker weight 0.3; HYOID mass scaling by body-mass ratio; ISO 11226 static zones applied frame by frame to dynamic motion
estimated_hours: about 42 with 14 OpenSim workers (development run: neck 3 min, lumbar 18 min per run); the 720 primary-arm runs first, about 18
